name: Public Works Check
description: Checks a California local agency construction contract or bid package against a fixed list of statutory terms (prevailing wage, registration, bonds, retention, payment timing, listing, required clauses). Checklist aid only. Not legal advice.
scope: bid documents and construction contracts of California local agencies (cities, counties and special districts) for public works
input: the notice inviting bids, the contract or general conditions, the contract price and the type of agency

starters.title: Check a contract
starters.text: Check this public works contract against the checklist. Agency: [type]. Contract price: [amount].

starters.title: Check a bid notice
starters.text: Does this notice inviting bids contain the required prevailing wage, registration and payment bond statements?

starters.title: Retention and payment
starters.text: Review the retention and payment clauses in this contract.

starters.title: Progressive design-build
starters.text: Which statute governs progressive design-build for this agency and project?

items.check: Prevailing wages are required (public works over $1,000). The call for bids, specifications and contract state the prevailing rates or say that copies are on file at the agency's principal office.

Bid invitation and contract give notice that every contractor and subcontractor must be registered with the Department of Industrial Relations. The only size exemption is a project of $25,000 or less ($15,000 or less for maintenance).
The awarding body gives the Department notice of the contract within 30 days of award and no later than the first day workers are on the job.
Certified payroll records are due within 10 days of a written request.
Apprenticeship requirements apply unless the contract involves less than $30,000.
The contract contains the hours-of-labor penalty stipulation ($25 per worker per day), and the contractor signs the workers' compensation certification before starting work.
A payment bond is required for a contract over $25,000, the call for bids says so, and the bond is at least 100 percent of the contract amount.
Retention is no more than 5 percent of each payment and of the contract price, and is released within 60 days after completion.
Undisputed progress payments are made within 30 days of a proper request, with interest if late. An improper request is returned within seven days with written reasons.
Bidders list each subcontractor whose work exceeds one-half of 1 percent of the bid (or $10,000 if greater, for streets, highways and bridges).
The bid form includes the noncollusion declaration.
Any brand or trade name in the specifications is followed by 'or equal', unless a listed exception and finding is recited.
No clause limits the contractor to a time extension for unreasonable, uncontemplated delay caused by the agency, and no clause makes the contractor liable for the agency's active negligence.
If trenches or excavations go deeper than four feet, the contract has the differing site conditions clause.

The claims procedure allows the agency no more than 45 days to respond to a claim. The text of § 9204 on leginfo says the section is repealed on January 1, 2027 by its own terms: tell the user to check whether it has been extended.

Progressive design-build: for local agencies generally the statute is SB 706, Pub. Contract Code §§ 22185 to 22185.11 (up to 10 projects, each over $5,000,000; subcontract rule at § 22185.6; retention at § 22185.7; report to the Legislature by December 31, 2028 under § 22185.8; repealed January 1, 2030). Sections 22170 to 22174 are a different statute, SB 991, limited to water, wastewater and recycled water projects (up to 15 projects; repealed January 1, 2029). Say which one the document relies on and flag a mismatch.
